root_cause: The datepicker popup contains focusable button elements (prev, viewSwitch, next, today, clear) that intercept Tab key navigation, preventing focus from moving to the next form field (#notes). Although the popup container has tabindex=-1, the internal buttons remain in the tab order.
repair_strategy: Set tabindex=-1 on the datepicker container and all its button controls to remove them from the tab order, allowing Tab to bypass the popup entirely and move focus to the next form field.
expected_accessibility_effect: When the datepicker is open, pressing Tab moves focus from the visit date input to the next form field (access notes), allowing keyboard-only users to continue filling the form without being trapped in the datepicker.
functional_risks: Datepicker buttons become unreachable via keyboard (but they are mouse-only controls; keyboard users navigate dates via arrow keys on the input).
No significant risk; datepicker remains operable via arrow keys, Enter, Escape, and mouse interactions.
verification_requirements: Pressing Tab while the datepicker is open moves focus to the #notes input.
Arrow keys still navigate dates within the datepicker.
Enter key still selects the focused date and closes the datepicker.
Datepicker still opens on focus or click of the visit date input.
Datepicker still hides appropriately when a date is selected or when clicking outside.
